hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Central America, bordering the North Pacific Ocean, between Guatemala and Honduras || mostly mountains with narrow coastal belt and central plateau || smallest Central American country and only one without a coastline on the Caribbean Sea || Resources: hydropower, geothermal power, petroleum, arable land || Exports: garments, plastic products, electrical capacitors, raw sugar, toilet paper (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: mostly mountains with narrow coastal belt and central plateau || Central America, bordering the North Pacific Ocean, between Guatemala and Honduras

climate.excerpt: tropical; rainy season (May to October); dry season (November to April); tropical on coast; temperate in uplands || known as the Land of Volcanoes; frequent and sometimes destructive earthquakes and volcanic activity; extremely susceptible to hurricanes volcanism: significant volcanic activity; San Salvador (1,893 m), which last erupted in 1917, has the potential to cause major harm to the country's capital, which lies just below the volcano's slopes; San Miguel (2,130 m) is one of the most active volcanoes in the country; other historically active volcanoes include Conchaguita, Ilopango, Izalco, and Santa Ana

economy.excerpt: upper-middle-income, dollarized Central American economy; reliant on remittances from US; recent growth linked to infrastructure investment, consumption, and crime reduction; $1.3 billion IMF loan to address fiscal imbalances; Bitcoin adopted as legal tender; persistent poverty and large informal sector || Exports: garments, plastic products, electrical capacitors, raw sugar, toilet paper (2023) || Industries: food processing, beverages, petroleum, chemicals, fertilizer, textiles, furniture, light metals
